feedback: If a learner sorts 'the bacteria tried to become resistant' as correct, flag that this credits the organism with lifetime, intentional change; the resistant variants were already present and simply left more offspring.

If the mechanism/result distinction is confused, clarify: selection is the differential survival and reproduction that happens each generation; evolution is the resulting change in heritable trait frequency across generations, which builds up over many generations.
Reward accounts that name which pre-existing variant was favoured and why it left more offspring, rather than ones that say the trait appeared because it helped.
activities.intendedInsight: The four conditions form a checklist that applies to any example, and correct accounts reason at the population level and distinguish mechanism from result; Lamarckian and need-driven phrasings can be identified and rejected.
learnerActions: Order the four conditions into the causal chain: variation → heritability → competition/over-reproduction → differential survival & reproduction → frequency change.
Given an account of antibiotic resistance, choose the correct population-level explanation over an incorrect Lamarckian alternative (e.g. 'the bacteria tried to become resistant').
Sort a set of statements about a case into 'correct natural-selection account' versus 'organism chose/needed to adapt'.

From before/after population descriptions, identify the mechanism (which pre-existing variants survived and reproduced more) and the result (the change in heritable trait frequency in later generations), noting that even a one-generation shift in heritable trait frequency is evolution, while large changes build up over many generations.
activities.title: Assemble and sort: the four conditions and correct-vs-Lamarckian accounts
